source.title: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day
source.author: Arnold Bennett
source.summary: A compact self-improvement book about treating time as the central asset and using nonworking hours for deliberate growth.
source.corePromise: Help readers reclaim ordinary days and turn spare time into self-development.

target.positioning: time, attention, energy, learning, and deep work for developers, founders, operators, and creators

us.evidence: Published in 1908 and available through public-domain digital editions.

adaptation.workingTitle: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day in the Age of Notifications
titleConcepts: How to Live on 24 Hours a Day in the Age of Notifications
subtitleOptions: A Modern Guide to Attention, Deep Work, Learning, and Daily Control
Arnold Bennett's Time Classic Rebuilt for Developers, Founders, and Creators
How to Reclaim Your Day From Work, Screens, and Drift
adaptation.modernWorld: Remote work, notifications, meetings, side projects, learning loops, commute time, AI tools, digital distraction, and knowledge-worker fatigue
toneRules: Write with practical sympathy for busy people.
Treat time as an asset without turning life into a productivity cult.
Make the plan small enough to execute and serious enough to matter.
prohibitedChanges: Do not shame readers for ordinary fatigue.
Do not promise extreme productivity hacks.
Do not imply Arnold Bennett wrote the adaptation.
coreLessons: Everyone receives the same daily time budget.
A job can consume energy without consuming the whole self.
Small protected blocks create real self-development.
Attention must be trained before time can be used well.
A sustainable program beats an ambitious collapse.
The goal is fuller living, not busier living.

chapterPlan.title: The Daily Allocation
chapterPlan.focus: Show that time is the one budget every reader receives equally.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: A knowledge worker loses the day to meetings, messages, and exhausted scrolling.

chapterPlan.title: The Second Day Hidden Inside the First
chapterPlan.focus: Recover evenings, mornings, commutes, and low-friction blocks.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: Modern workers build a personal day around the workday.

chapterPlan.title: Protect Ninety Minutes
chapterPlan.focus: Translate Bennett's small-start program into deep work and skill growth.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: A founder or developer uses small blocks for writing, learning, selling, or building.

chapterPlan.title: Train the Attention Layer
chapterPlan.focus: Update concentration practice for phones, tabs, and context switching.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: Notification hygiene, monotasking, and deliberate study.

chapterPlan.title: Do Not Overbuild the System
chapterPlan.focus: Warn against productivity systems that collapse under their own weight.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: Apps, dashboards, trackers, and plans that become procrastination.

chapterPlan.title: A Life That Fits Inside the Day
chapterPlan.focus: Tie time discipline to fuller living and self-respect.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: The reader builds a life outside reactive work.
